routes.description: Establish that observed change, causal dependence, natural order, abstract reality, and objective moral obligation require an ultimate actual, necessary, intelligent, and morally authoritative source properly identified as God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if at least one developed natural-theology inference establishes a necessary divine source and the account can connect that source to the relevant divine attributes while answering methodological and moral alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Show that the best ultimate explanation of the burden-relevant features of reality is an actual, necessary divine intellect rather than an unexplained natural terminus.

centralBridges.description: Derive a purely actual or necessary first source from change, instrumental causation, contingency, and the claimed impossibility of an infinite regress of unrealized potency.
Connect natural regularity, goal-directed behavior, universals, and sufficient explanation to an ordering intellect beyond dependent nature.
Establish that genuinely objective moral obligations exist independently of human preference and require grounding in a divine intellect.
Explain why the ultimate source reached by the arguments possesses enough unity, necessity, intellect, authority, and transcendence to be identified as God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend natural theology as a legitimate inference from observable effects to an extranatural explanation, including the disputed analogy with scientific reasoning.
Reconcile divine goodness and hiddenness with evil, imperfect creation, free agency, greater goods, limited perspective, and interpersonal knowledge of God.

routes.description: Maintain that the affirmative has not supplied a defined, demonstrable, and evidentially supported God conclusion because its causal, scientific, moral, and personal-experience inferences admit gaps or secular alternatives, while divine hiddenness supplies an independent skeptical consideration.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative inferences do not warrant the transition from observed phenomena to the claimed God, especially under a revisable evidence standard, or if expected divine disclosure conflicts with the available public evidence.

motionBridge.description: Show that neither the offered proofs nor alleged revelation provides sufficient warrant for accepting that the God described in the motion exists.

centralBridges.description: Require a sufficiently defined God claim and a valid, supported demonstration while distinguishing withheld belief from a burden to prove exhaustive nonexistence.
Challenge extrapolation from intracosmic causation to an atemporal first cause and the further identification of any explanatory terminus with a divine mind.
Require proposed extranatural causes to be independently demonstrable rather than inferred solely from unresolved cosmology, model singularities, or gaps in natural explanation.
Account for moral assessment through stipulated goals, well-being, physical facts, and shared conventions without positing an independently existing divine moral law.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test personal-God conceptions against the expectation that a capable deity wanting belief would provide clear, verifiable, and sufficient disclosure.
Separate atheism's position on divine existence from the broader ethical, epistemic, and purposive commitments supplied by skepticism, humanism, or other views.

sections.title: Burden of Proof, Public Evidence, and Divine Hiddenness
sections.rationale: This issue fixes the warrant required for the motion, the relationship between affirmative proof and skeptical withholding, and whether expected divine disclosure supplies an independent consideration about a personal God.

sections.title: Thomistic Causation and Identification of the First Source
sections.rationale: The transition from change, potency, causation, and contingency to a purely actual necessary source is a principal affirmative path, while identifying that source as the God at issue is a distinct indispensable step.

sections.title: Natural Theology, Cosmology, and Extranatural Explanation
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether inference to the best explanation may include extranatural causes and whether cosmological singularities or other scientific models support rather than merely leave open such explanations.

sections.title: Moral Objectivity, Secular Foundations, and Divine Grounding
sections.rationale: The moral-law route depends on objective obligation existing beyond human preference and requiring divine grounding, while the opposing route offers goal-relative objective assessment and contests that ontological inference.

sections.title: Divine Attributes, Evil, and Interpersonal Knowledge
sections.rationale: The motion requires connecting an ultimate source to recognizably divine attributes and addressing whether evil, imperfect creation, private conviction, or interpersonal knowledge coheres with and warrants belief in that God.
